_note: Map v4's road surface model and everything made from it (MAP_README.md; map/model/). Every width, spacing, threshold and tolerance the v4 bake uses. Bump version after changing anything: the next bake redoes every tile and the game's tile cache drops the old ones. Map v3's own settings stay in data/map/bake.json (still read for terrain colours, surfaces, barriers, trees' density, buildings).

graph._note: densify: m between points added on gentle curves (OSM's own nodes never move); straightSpacing: m between points along straight pieces (for the height profile); maxTurnPerPoint: degrees a curve may turn between two points before more are added; corner: a turn sharper than this (degrees) stays a corner; jointMaxTurn: two roads meeting end to end turning more than this (degrees) get a junction patch instead of a shared cross-section; jointMaxWidthChange: m of width change a shared cross-section takes (more: a patch); borderNodes: a graph node where a road crosses a tile border

widths._note: Each road's width (m): the OSM width tag when there is one (the carriageway, kerb to kerb), else lanes × laneWidth + both shoulders, else the class's lanes (twoWay / oneWay: per direction on a one-way carriageway). visual = drivable + 2 × kerb (the kerb band is drawn, flush). multiplier: everything (1.0 is real size with these generous defaults). minDrivable: never narrower. Lanes and widths not tagged in OSM are marked estimated.
widths._sideBySide: Roads side by side that don't meet there (two carriageways of one road, a service road beside a street): the sides facing each other are narrowed so a gap of at least medianMin m stays between them (the real median kept, not filled), never below minHalf m from the centre line; eased along the road over easeLength m. Marked adjusted.

heights._note: The road surface's heights, solved on the graph, from the elevation opened over demOpen m (what's left of buildings and trees in a surface model, bumps narrower than that, cut off) and blurred over demBlur m (the source is 30 m): each way's elevation profile (spikes out: a running median over `median` points either side; then a Gaussian, `smooth` m) → junction heights and planes (the profiles' heights where they reach the junction, a least-squares plane through them no steeper than junctionMaxSlope) → each segment bent to meet its ends, then held to maxGrade and to maxGradeChange (change of grade per metre: no crest that throws a car) by relaxation. Neighbouring junctions' planes are relaxed towards each other (planePasses) until the road between any two is no steeper than planeGrade (planeFollowsGround: or rather rises as the ground does there, within planeGrade). shortRoadCurve: a road between two planes shorter than two eases made one smooth curve meeting both planes' heights and slopes (else eased from each end). armEase: m over which (on a road shorter than twice it, half its length from each end) a road eases from its own profile and camber onto a junction's plane. Bridges ease straight between their ends and are lifted overpassClearance over what they cross; tunnels likewise below.

junctions._note: Junction patches: each arm trimmed back to where its edges meet its neighbours' (plus kerbRadius, the corner's round), at least minTrim m, at most maxTrim m and never into the next junction (then the two become one cluster with one patch). A corner where the edges meet ahead is a curve round kerbRadius; one where they don't (a straight run past, the wide side of a fork) follows the edges round. minRibbon: the least road left between two junctions' trims before they merge. mergeDistance: junction nodes this close always share a patch. Holes in a patch smaller than minHoleArea m² or thinner than minHoleWidth m (on average) are slivers, filled; bigger ones are islands and medians, kept. closeGap: cracks in a patch's outline narrower than this (m) are closed (0: off — Clipper's offsets leave artefacts on dense curves).

surface._note: The surface's cross-section: visual edge, kerb's inner edge (drivable edge), half way, crown — mirrored. skirtDepth: a strip down from the visual edge (drawn only, not solid) so the ground's sink never shows as a gap. Dead ends run capLength m past their last node. Markings (cheap: one vertex-coloured mesh) by region style; lines markingWidth m wide, raised markingLift m, dashed dash/gap m. easeRows: m from a trim where a road's rows are, through its ease onto the junction's plane (closer near the trim). quantum: every vertex put on this grid (m: the tiles' position quantum) before T-junctions are closed, so the ones closed stay closed in the tiles.

terrain._note: The ground under and round the road surface, in the height grid itself (so the drawn ground and the physics' heightfield match): every grid point under the surface or within margin m of it set sink m under the nearest road surface (margin is at least the grid cell's diagonal: no terrain triangle can reach up into the road); then sloping back to the natural ground (1 : slope, minBlend to maxBlend m). The terrain's simplified meshes are cut, under and beside the roads (the exclusion mask's road and buffer), from the heights lowered by their own error and lodRoadDrop m more, so they can't come up through a road at any distance (the physics keeps the grid as it is). Bridges: the ground kept bridgeClearance under the deck (underBridge away from its ends). Tunnels: the ground over them kept as a roof.

collision._note: Road collision: each tile's road triangles plus apron m of its neighbours' past its edge (overlapping copies of the same surface: no edge at the border for a wheel or the car's body to catch), as one trimesh with Rapier's internal-edge fix. Building colliders never on a road: a hull over the road surface (any point of it within roadClearance m) is trimmed back off it, or dropped if too little is left (logged). Bumps: the most vertical acceleration (m/s², the car's body, beyond gravity) allowed crossing junctions, bridge ends and tile borders.

exclusion._note: The exclusion mask (baked, inspectable): a 1 m raster of where nothing may stand — every road surface on every layer plus buffer m, junctions, car parks, tunnel portals (portal m round each end), railways (railway m each side), and the ground under every bridge deck plus deckMargin m. A tree is placed only if no masked cell is under its crown (crownRadius × its scale); under a deck only if allowUnderDecks and its crown's top is clearance m under the deck (the clearance stored in the data). Lamps and signs: their foot.

lamps._note: Street lamps: OSM's (highway=street_lamp, man_made=street_lamp) first; then estimated ones from the road model on lit roads (lit=yes; the alwaysLitClasses — main roads, lit through parks too; or urban classes when lit isn't tagged, in built-up areas; never lit=no): spacing m by kind, at the kerb (offset m outside the visual edge) or in a median wider than medianMin m, both sides of roads at least bothSidesWidth m wide; one at every junction corner of a lit road, two at crossings; tunnels continuous at tunnel m, on the wall. Never in a lane, on a road surface, or under a deck (the exclusion mask). A mapped lamp within mappedRadius m stands in for an estimated one. Height, arm, colour, and the rendering's real-light count.

barriers._note: Railings from the model: OSM's barrier lines (never on a road surface: each piece tested along its whole length against the exclusion mask), and estimated ones (flagged) both sides of bridges, motorway edges, medians at least median m wide, and road edges with the ground dropping more than drop m within reach m for at least minRun m (none within skipNearJunction m of a junction patch). Chained with no gaps.

bake._note: workers: tiles written in parallel (0: one per core less one); gzip level (9 is 3% smaller and twice as slow as 6)

tests._note: Map v4's tests (tests/map/v4.test.ts): the limits each measurement is held to. widthShare: the drawn road at least this share of the model's width (5th percentile). maxCracksPer100k: T-junction cracks inside the road (a vertex of one piece within 3 mm of another's edge but not on it, road all round it) in the joined tiles' road surface, per 100,000 triangles — notches in the road's outline aren't counted. maxOverlapShare: road surface sampled with two solid layers within 0.5 m of each other. edgeInset/edgeSpacing: road edges sampled this far inside the drawn edge, this often (m); maxHoleShare: of those with no drawn road; maxGroundThroughShare: with the drawn ground over the road (near and middle detail); maxPhysicsGap: the collision surface this close to the drawn one (m). maxStep: a junction's join (m, beyond the road's own grade) — at most maxStepShare of the samples across joins over it, maxJoinHoleShare with no road. bumpSpeeds: km/h for the bump runs, bumpLimits the most vertical acceleration (m/s²) at each — 150 km/h through a city junction that follows the real grade can't be under 2.5 g. lampCoverage: the share of lit-class road with a lamp within lampReach m. badSpotRadius: m round each known bad spot re-checked. surfaceTiles: how many tiles (round the spawn and the bad spots) are joined for the watertight check; auditTiles: how many have every collider audited (all of them in a slice).
